authorization: Standing autonomous approval; decisions and limitations recorded for later review.

policy.reference_basis: Keep each caller signed physical quantity, formula and supported uncertainty exactly; only supplier identity changes for useful-heat MJ. No efficiency or loss is applied again.
policy.classification: Exact provider identities only. Industrial furnaces, chemical heat and allocated plant heat proxy industrial final heat. Small/central boilers, domestic fuel cells and heat pumps proxy buildings final heat. Explicit delivered district heat uses complete native delivery, never the transport-only network service. Consumer use may differ from source technology class; this is an explicit screening boundary.
policy.protected_inventory: Keep all CLIC source records, Brightpath migration helpers, scenario heat-owned records and native MJ/kWh energy-reference inventories unchanged. This preserves direct generation/combustion/network inventories; infrastructure and other material-producing consumers can change upstream heat supply.
policy.retained_boundaries: Keep network-only, ambient heat-extraction components and mass-based steam supplies. Native steam uses fuel-input MJ services; no useful-heat conversion has been established here. These retained services remain historical and are not claimed updated. Retain the explicitly documented zero-allocated MSWI heat handover and all its signed uses; do not turn a burden-free allocated handover into an avoided IAM mix.
policy.geography: Use the consumer IAM region where that layer exists; otherwise use the delivered-volume-weighted World fallback with a literal geographic-proxy audit. Missing entire IAM layers are explicitly non-applicable; industrial inputs may use secondary supply only when industrial end-use data are absent, matching existing supply-only behavior.

limitations: Heat grade, temperature, pressure, quality, technology class, on-site/purchased boundary, source geography, vintage, coproduct allocation and internal uncertainty differ. IAM role assumptions and supplier limitations remain; score effects are unquantified.

Replacing recovered or allocated heat inputs with an IAM mix changes the credit/supply basis. Preserve every signed caller quantity; do not alter treatment inputs, emissions or add avoided-emission credits.

Native heat/electricity and combustion inventories and all CLIC/helper records stay complete. Native steam, environmental heat components and network-only supplies remain historical at this stage. No claim of complete heat decarbonization or LCIA equivalence.
